public_sources.observed_contract: Update-ref accepts target SHA plus force flag. force=false requires fast-forward behavior; force=true permits non-fast-forward movement. The endpoint documents conflict/validation outcomes but no caller-supplied generation-floor predicate or effect-id uniqueness predicate.

Create-status is append-style for a SHA/context and permits up to 1000 statuses per SHA/context. Request fields are state, target_url, description and context; the documented endpoint has no conditional generation-floor compare or effect-id uniqueness predicate.

Rulesets can restrict updates/deletions and block force pushes, but creating/editing/deleting repository rulesets requires repository admin access or a custom role with edit-repository-rules permission. Protected-branch restrictions can also have bypass actors/admin behavior.

candidate_matrix.G1: pass for the exposed ref-write primitive itself
candidate_matrix.G2: pass only as lightweight repository transport; ordinary API rate limits remain a checkpoint/fail-closed transport concern rather than accepted compute
candidate_matrix.reason: Fast-forward checking constrains one ref transition but does not atomically compare an application generation floor and a single-use effect_id. The same GitHub contract exposes force=true, so the ref is not rollback-independent under an authority domain that permits forced rewind; delete/recreate is likewise not represented by a durable sink-local minimum-generation witness.

candidate_matrix.candidate: commit status stream attached to immutable commit SHA
candidate_matrix.G1: fail in the current Chat connector because status creation is not exposed; public API would additionally require commit-status write permission
candidate_matrix.G2: fail the strict zero-exhaustible-limit test as a universal witness because GitHub documents a finite 1000-status-per-SHA/context limit
candidate_matrix.reason: Multiple statuses for one SHA/context are explicitly allowed up to the limit, so repeated logical effect markers are not rejected by uniqueness. Status creation has no documented generation-floor conditional predicate. Attachment to a commit SHA can survive a branch rewind as historical metadata, but that alone is not atomic anti-rollback plus dedupe authority.

candidate_matrix.G3: fail as a complete sink protocol
candidate_matrix.reason: Creating/editing repository rulesets requires admin or edit-repository-rules authority, which violates this CLEAN leaf's no protected/admin/manual setup gate. Even a protected ref prevents a class of ref rewrites rather than atomically consuming an application effect_id together with generation-floor validation.

observations: GitHub's ref API documents force=false fast-forward protection and an explicit force=true mode.
GitHub's commit-status API documents up to 1000 statuses per SHA/context and does not expose generation-floor/effect-id conditional fields.
GitHub's ruleset documentation says repository rulesets require admin access or a custom role with edit-repository-rules permission to create/edit/delete.
The current Chat GitHub connector exposes update_ref but not commit-status creation or ruleset mutation.
inferences: No inspected GitHub-native alternative is a concrete rollback-domain-independent authoritative sink that atomically enforces {generation >= durable minimum AND effect_id unused} under the current CLEAN role gates.
This is a bounded capability-gap result, not a proof that every possible GitHub feature or every non-GitHub mechanism is impossible.

phase1_leaf_result.minimal_unresolved_child: A role-permitted Chat-native authority outside the ordinary repository rollback domain that durably and atomically rejects both stale generation (generation < minimum) and repeated logical effect_id without protected/admin/manual setup, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental monetary cost.
phase1_leaf_result.narrowed_finding: Git ref CAS/fast-forward is useful as a local concurrency fence but is not the missing rollback-independent generation+effect sink. Commit statuses and rulesets also fail at least one hard gate in current scope.

scope_guard: Only the three named official GitHub surfaces, current connector action inventory, and seven constructed probes were evaluated. No claim is made about undocumented semantics, enterprise-only controls not inspected, arbitrary connectors, or every external sink.
continuation: Part103: execute exactly one bounded co-rollback indistinguishability leaf. Model two histories that produce identical observable repository plus role-local state at invocation start: H0 never advanced beyond generation g3; H1 advanced to g4, emitted/authorized a g4 effect, then every repository-visible authority, marker, ref and role-local witness in the same rollback domain was restored to the exact H0 image. For deterministic repository-only protocols, test the safety/availability tradeoff: accepting g3 in H0 versus rejecting stale g3 in H1. Determine the narrowest theorem scope, then test whether content-addressed effect naming or append-only non-authoritative evidence changes the result without introducing a rollback-independent authority. Persist the exact counterexample or scope-limited escape hatch and a nonempty next-invocation continuation; do not generalize beyond the finite observation model.
